title: Query plan regression after a statistics refresh turns a hot query into a sequential scan
source_note: Failure pattern (an ANALYZE / statistics update flips the planner from an index scan to a sequential scan on a large table, so a frequently-run query becomes very slow and saturates database CPU) is a common query-plan-regression class. All services, query names, row counts, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~08:00 UTC the dashboards are timing out and anything sharing the reporting database is slow. Database CPU is near 100%. No deploys. There was a large data import into the reporting database earlier.

signal_lines.msg: auto-analyze ran on table events after a bulk import (~30M new rows)
query q_dashboard_summary latency 8s+ (baseline ~40ms); now doing a sequential scan on events (200M rows)
dashboard requests timing out; DB CPU 96%
plan regression confirmed: q_dashboard_summary switched from index scan to seq scan after the stats update
other queries sharing the database are slow due to CPU contention from the sequential scans
pinned the index plan for q_dashboard_summary; latency back to ~45ms

ground_truth.root_cause: A routine auto-analyze, triggered after a ~30M-row bulk import into the events table, updated the table statistics, and the query planner then switched a frequently-run dashboard query (q_dashboard_summary) from an index scan to a sequential scan on the 200M-row events table. That query's latency jumped from ~40ms to over 8s, and the repeated sequential scans drove database CPU to 96%, slowing every other query sharing the database. There was no deploy - the trigger was the statistics refresh changing the plan. Recovery required pinning the good (index) plan for that query.
evidence_path: reporting-db INFO ~10 min before onset: auto-analyze ran on the events table after a ~30M-row bulk import
reporting-db WARN: q_dashboard_summary latency 8s+ vs a ~40ms baseline, now doing a sequential scan on events (200M rows)
reporting-db ERROR: plan regression confirmed - the query switched from index scan to seq scan after the stats update
db_cpu_utilization climbs to 96% from the repeated sequential scans; other queries slow from contention
latency returns to ~45ms after the plan is pinned for that query
ground_truth.fix: Pin the index plan for q_dashboard_summary (done). Investigate why the planner's cost estimate favoured a seq scan after ANALYZE (stale or skewed stats, missing extended statistics), add plan-regression monitoring on the top queries, and control when ANALYZE runs on large tables after bulk imports.
